newsitem.title: USA: U.S. high court to decide case over 1865 shipwreck.
newsitem.headline: U.S. high court to decide case over 1865 shipwreck.

text.p: The Supreme Court said Monday it would decide an ownership dispute involving an 1865 shipwreck off the California coast.

A firm called Deep Sea Research initially claimed salvage rights and title to the wreck of the Brother Jonathan, a double-paddle steamer that sank off Crescent City. After 19 years of searching the firm claimed in 1994 to have discovered the ship, located on the submerged land of California.

California then intervened in the court case, asserting it has a claim of ownership to the wreck under a federal abandoned shipwreck law and under state law. But a federal judge ruled that the state had failed to establish a claim to ownership and the ruling was upheld by a U.S. appeals court.

California, supported by 15 other states, appealed to the Supreme Court, saying the lower court was wrong and should be overruled. The justices will hear arguments and decide the case during the court's 1997-98 term that begins in October.
